author: United States (compiled laws)

locator: "An Act fixing the Military Peace Establishment of the United States" (approved 16 March 1802), Sec. 8, printed p. 53: the annual uniform clothing of non-commissioned officers, musicians and privates of the artillery and infantry.
rights_note: A United States statute printed in 1812; public domain. Used only for the list of uniform clothing a private drew each year (T-3451).
access_notes: Read 2026-11-07 (T-3451) in the scan's full text. Sec. 8: every non-commissioned officer, musician and private of the artillery and infantry shall receive annually "one hat, one coat, one vest, two pair of woollen and two pair linen overalls, one coarse linen frock and trowsers for fatigue clothing, four pair of shoes, four shirts, two pair of socks, two pair of short stockings, one blanket, one stock and clasp, and one pair of half gaiters". Still the law in this 1812 compilation.
note: The issue a private of the First Infantry drew in 1812; it names the pieces, not their cut or colour.
what_it_supplies: the pieces of a private's issue in 1812: hat, coat, vest, woollen and linen overalls, shoes, stock and clasp, half gaiters
what_it_does_not_supply: the cut, colour or facings of any piece
what the Fort Dearborn garrison actually had in August 1812
